title: 2018 AMC 10B Problem 25
statement: Let \(\lfloor x \rfloor\) denote the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x.\) How many real numbers \(x\) satisfy the equation \(x^2 + 10{,}000\lfloor x \rfloor = 10{,}000x?\)

solutions.text: Let \(a = \lfloor x \rfloor.\) The equation reads \(x^2 = 10{,}000(x - a)\) \(= 10{,}000\{x\},\) and since \(0 \le \{x\} < 1,\) this forces \(0 \le x^2 < 10{,}000,\) so \(-100 < x < 100.\) On each interval \([a, a + 1)\) the quantity \(10{,}000x - x^2\) increases from \(10{,}000a - a^2\) and approaches, but does not reach, \(10{,}000(a+1) - (a+1)^2.\) It hits \(10{,}000a\) exactly once precisely when \((a + 1)^2 < 10{,}000.\) That holds for the integers \(-100 \le a \le 98,\) which is \(199\) solutions. Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Writing \(\{x\} = x - \lfloor x \rfloor,\) the equation is \(x^2 = 10{,}000\{x\},\) so \(0 \le x^2 < 10{,}000\)
On each interval \([a, a+1)\) there is a solution exactly when \((a + 1)^2 \lt 10{,}000\)
